behavior: ADR-017 records the scoped firewall decision as Amendment B
On an iptables host setup appends the rule scoped to tailscale0, in exactly the form iptables -S prints it
An unscoped allow for the port is legacy; a scoped, source-limited or port-less one is not
Setup replaces the exact legacy copies (scoped rule first, delete after), reports any other unscoped allow as manual, and deletes nothing when the add fails
Check reports a legacy unscoped iptables rule and firewall_ok is false until it is gone
On a real iptables host setup converges, a second run changes nothing, and a hand-added legacy rule is reported then replaced
Every ufw write is `allow in on tailscale0 to any port N proto tcp`, from one helper
An unscoped ufw allow for the port is legacy; a scoped, commented or multi-port one is not exact
On a ufw host setup replaces the legacy allow (scoped first, delete after) and reports other unscoped allows as manual
The Windows recreate carries -RemoteAddress for the tailnet ranges and no longer enables the built-in Remote Desktop group
Check compares the rule's RemoteAddress as a normalized set; a rule open to any address is reported as legacy and recreated scoped
On a real Windows host setup writes the scoped rule and repairs a legacy one (pending: the Windows guest is shared)
